Indian citizen
2. Minimum 18 years of age (no upper age limit)
3. Minimum 10th grade (or equivalent)
4. Minimum 12th grade (or equivalent)
5. Minimum 3 years of experience in the pharmaceutical industry (or 2 years in a related field)
6. No disqualifying criminal record | | **Qualification** | 10th + 12th + 3 years experience (or 2 years experience + 12th) | | **Exam Dates** | Preliminary: ~April 2026
Main: ~June 2026 (exact dates announced by UPSC) | | **Exam Pattern** | **Preliminary** – 2 objective papers (each 100 marks, 2‑minute per question)
**Main** – 2 descriptive papers (each 200 marks, 3‑hour duration) | | **Syllabus** | 1. **Preliminary** – General Studies (current affairs, Indian polity, economy, science & technology, environment, etc.)
2. **Main** –
• *Paper‑I*: Drug Inspection & Regulatory Affairs (200 marks)
• *Paper‑II*: Pharmaceutical Quality Assurance & Good Manufacturing Practices (200 marks) | | **Important Topics** | • Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 & Rules
• Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP)
• Good Laboratory Practices (GLP)
• Good Clinical Practices (GCP)
• Pharmacovigilance
• Quality Control & Assurance
• Regulatory submissions & approvals
• Current affairs in pharma & healthcare | | **Preparation Tips** | 1. **Start Early** – Begin with the UPSC syllabus and build a study plan.

3. **Industry Knowledge** – Read industry reports, regulatory updates, and case studies.
